key_insight: Paying for a better LLM is task-dependent: adaptive oracle switching can meet downstream optimization accuracy targets at lower cumulative cost than fixed high-fidelity choices.
engineering_relevance: LLM-assisted data-curation pipelines can choose model fidelity according to downstream optimization needs rather than always using the most expensive model.
method: With known bias, use a restarted, cost-aware policy to select oracle fidelity across optimization stages.
With unknown bias, use occasional trusted-gradient evaluations to certify progress and eliminate unsuccessful oracle sources.
Instantiate the frameworks with biased stochastic gradient extrapolation and recursive regularization under state-dependent noise.
evidence_signal: Synthetic and LLM-completion experiments show adaptive switching skipping several expensive LLM oracles and substantially reducing cumulative cost while achieving accuracy comparable to fixed high-fidelity alternatives.
watch_item: When bias is unknown, trusted-gradient certification adds cost, and less frequent checks can delay detection of biased sources.
paper_title: When is a better LLM worth paying for? Stochastic Optimization with Switching Mixed-Fidelity Oracles
